messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed p99 token latency in eu-west jump from ~180ms to ~450ms over the last 20m while tokens/sec stayed flat. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/rdw-token-slo/eu-west-token-slo :eyes:
ops-bot: ALERT: token_latency_p99{region="eu-west"} > 400ms for 3m — firing (alert 1321)
kenji: investigating, grabbing node and pod lists. initial quick check: two serving pods on west2-azc show rx_err and NIC retries. pulling logs now.
anil: can you paste the PromQL you used for the p99 panel? want to reproduce locally.
kenji: PromQL I'm using on the panel: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, pod, region))` — then we roll up by region. also looking at `sum by(pod) (rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[10m]))`
dasha: on my side I'm seeing a correlated uptick in avg sequence length for that cohort — a few customers with long prompts started ramping. could be kv-cache churn + bigger KV lookups amplifying tail latency.
maria: good call. can we slice p99 by seq_len buckets and by model_variant? a small number of long-seq requests could blow up p99 while tokens/sec looks normal.
kenji: adding a panel now: `sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, seq_bucket)` and a tokens/sec heatmap by shard. initial slice shows p99 dominated by seq_len > 2048 requests on two pods.
anil: thinking alert tuning: current p99 alert is global and too sensitive to rare long sequences. propose change: alert only when p99 > 400ms AND tokens/sec_region > 5k OR p99 sustained > 400ms for 15m. plus a cardinality guard on pod count to avoid noisy microspikes.
maria: agreed. also add a cost-aware metric: normalized_tail = p99_latency / max(1, tokens/sec_region) so we can detect unit-cost regressions. add to Optimize team dashboard.
dasha: while we dig traces, enable higher tracing sample rate for eu-west (25%) for next 2h so we capture these long-seq traces. I'll flip the sampler and post link to traces.
kenji: flipped sampler. captured few traces — looks like KV cache miss rate correlates with a KV eviction storm: `kv_cache_evictions_total` jumps right before the tail latencies.
maria: that points to caching pressure. short-term mitigation: can we increase cache capacity on those pods or pin the long-seq customers to warm shards?
kenji: we can nudge routing for ~5% of traffic to eu-central to relieve west until infra can adjust. will open a routing canary (5% -> eu-central) and monitor p99.
anil: for alerts, I'll open a PR to modify the alert rule: add `and sum(rate(tokens_total[5m])) by (region) > 5000` and change forgroup to 900s. also add optional `for: >2m` on pod-level alerts.
dasha: created a short-lived dashboard panel that shows p99 vs kv_evictions merged; screenshot uploaded to the thread.
maria: sounds good. if p99 doesn't drop after canary and cache bump, escalate to eng-infra to look at NIC kernel stats (we saw rx_err). I'll file an incident if persists past 30m.
kenji: canary was applied 2m ago — eu-west p99 dropped from 450ms -> 220ms so far. continuing to watch.
maria: great — keep the higher trace sampling until we have a postmortem. add a note to the ticket about cost impact (extra traces + canary bandwidth) so finance can track. :memo:
ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: manual canary routing applied by kenji at 1876543375 — shifting 5% to eu-central.
maria: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) anil: PR for alert tuning, (2) kenji: cache capacity tweak and follow-up telemetry, (3) dasha: trace samples + short postmortem draft. Back here in 1h for status. :thumbsup:
